originalText:
On Figma Motion, my demo & review. 

This is one of those updates that clicked swiftly into my workflow. Like in my 3D pipeline, using this stick shift animation, I emphasize hardware feedback with motion from Figma Motion. 

Assets are animated in Fig Motion and loaded into Blender as video textures for mesh and material control. 

It's advantageous since it is built into an ubiquitous ecosystem. A lot of work these days start in Figma even for someone like me that works outside the tool frequently. 

Can't over-emphasize my appreciation for the schema used to introduce motion to nearly all properties. Reminds me of how motion works in Blender - with better complexity management. Better than introducing more menus for those. Ease curves iD between keyframes is also an improvement over existing systems. 

Having spent some time on the tool, here are updates I'll like to see to Figma Motion. These are based on my immediate needs as at the time of working on this demo:

• Using modifier keys (CMD, Shift, Ctrl) to jump / nudge across the timeline. E.g: holding down Shift key to make the playhead jump 100ms etc.

• Jump to previous or next keyframe.

• Better anchor point trails

• Renaming layers from the timeline as well.

• Editable custom bezier styles: after saving a style, I should be able to edit the curve - just as you can edit colour styles.

• Enable transform on the timeline. I should be able to flip or scale keyframes.

I hope to continue trying more ideas. Craft focused tools have had to take a backseat in recent times. Pleasing to see this come to light.

originalText:
Just tried the AI agent for motion in @figma 

As expected, it's far from great

But it's not completely useless

It can do simple slideshows, mass update keyframes, easing, etc

Good way to eliminate repetitive work

This is the prompt i used btw:

Showcase animation: move the group to reveal each child frame one at a time, centered in the viewport. Jump between frames in a non-sequential order so the camera feels like it's exploring, no row-by-row pattern. Use smooth, human-like panning: gentle ease-in out of rest, long deceleration into each stop (cubic bezier ~0.4, 0, 0.2, 1). Hold each frame briefly before moving on. At the end, pan back to the first frame so the animation loops seamlessly

originalText:
✅ 피그마의 새 기능, Motion 소개

Config 2026에서 공개된 Figma Motion이에요(현재 오픈 베타)
- 디자인하던 캔버스 안에서 모션까지 바로 만드는 기능
- Design·Draw·Dev 옆에 생긴 Motion 모드에서 사용 가능

📍 Motion으로 할 수 있는 작업:
- 타임라인에서 위치·크기·회전·투명도를 키프레임으로 잡고, 프리셋으로 빠르게 시작
- 모션이 처음이면 에이전트에 말로 설명하면, 컴포넌트·토큰에 맞춰 키프레임을 생성
- 컴포넌트에 모션을 한 번 입히면 색·글꼴처럼 모든 화면과 협업자 파일로 전파 (디자인 시스템의 일부로)
- Dev 모드에서 타임라인 그대로 열어 CSS·JSON·React로 복사, MCP로 코딩 에이전트에 전달
- MP4·GIF·WebM·Animated SVG로 내보내기

기본 기능은 모든 플랜에서 써볼 수 있고, 애니메이션 컴포넌트 공유·모션 에이전트·고해상도 내보내기는 유료 플랜용입니다

A lot of people using Figma Motion still don’t know about anchor point control and path-based object animation.

And honestly, those 2 things alone can make your motion feel way more intentional.

Most people just animate from point A to point B.

But once you understand how to:

- rotate an object from a specific anchor point
​- make an object feel like it’s moving along a path
- fake path animation even when it’s not natively there

Here's a quick breakdown on how to do both in Figma Motion.

If you’ve been using Motion but haven’t explored anchor points or path-style movement yet, you’re probably missing some of its most useful capabilities.
